- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 2–3 days post-spike.
- Model frequently overpredicts in early horizon (e.g., 1–7 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or mixed; apply a 1–2% downward bias for short-term forecasts.
- In high volatility periods (e.g., sentiment swings >0.5), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to match recent 3–5 day moving average for better alignment.
- When sentiment is stable (0.33–0.67) and price is trending sideways, model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply a 1–3% downward bias to avoid overconfidence in continuation.
